A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 18-page versions of Learning a Game by Paying the Agents, with matching Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–D. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 presents algorithms, theoretical guarantees, proofs, and constructed game examples. Neither the main text nor Appendices A–D report experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 retains the theoretical treatment and constructed examples, with no original empirical outcomes in the main text or appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain identical payment updates, signaling procedures, utility estimation, and steering steps. The models and algorithmic components are unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation tasks. The theoretical single-agent, multi-agent, and steering settings are unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version reports experimentally evaluated baselines. The alternative algorithms and theoretical comparisons discussed in Sections 4–5 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an empirical evaluation protocol. No experimental splits, metrics, budgets, sample sizes, or testing procedures are added or revised.

E4.justification: The supplementary theoretical analyses and constructed game example in Appendices A–D are unchanged. No ablation, sensitivity, robustness, or error study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The theoretical discussion of high-probability regret guarantees is unchanged.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical scores, rankings, or observed findings. The illustrative payoffs in Appendix D.2 are unchanged; the asymptotic lower-bound correction is assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.4 changes its first lower-bound term from Omega(nM) log(1/epsilon) to tilde-Omega(nM) log(1/epsilon). Its proof sketch also restores log(1/epsilon) in the required information count. These corrections align the statement and sketch with the unchanged Appendix C.2 derivation, which divides by log M. The C^2/(4epsilon^2) term and full proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: Section 6 narrows the stated utility-learning bottleneck from Omega(nM) log(1/epsilon) to tilde-Omega(nM) log(1/epsilon). The abstract, introductory informal theorems, and principal learning and steering contributions are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretation of utility learning as a potential steering bottleneck and the associated open question remain unchanged. Explanations of signaling, history dependence, applicability limits, and other future directions are also retained.

D1.justification: Algorithm pseudocode, step sizes, parameter choices, and the linear program for computing optimal CEPs are unchanged. No implementation details or code/data access information are added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 and the references retain the same cited works and research positioning. No literature coverage or novelty comparison changes.

P1.justification: Localized edits affect Theorem 4.4's statement and proof sketch and the final future-work bullet. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The corrected formulas produce small line-wrapping and vertical-spacing changes on pages 7 and 10. No figures, tables, or algorithm displays are added or redesigned, and all appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects an overstated lower bound in Theorem 4.4 and the conclusion and restores the missing precision factor in the proof sketch. This brings the main text into agreement with Appendix C.2, improving mathematical accuracy and internal consistency. The improvement is limited because the algorithms, full proofs, and broader contributions remain unchanged.
